state.case_summary:
A 47-year-old Japanese male employed at a food company reported experiencing bloody discharge from the left nipple. The patient has a history of hypospadias, which is also present in one male relative. There is no family history of breast cancer. The patient underwent two plastic surgeries for hypospadias at ages 4-5 and four additional surgeries at ages 20-21. The patient appears male and has male sterility, with no history of trauma to the external genitalia or mumps. Upon noticing the bloody discharge from the left nipple, the patient sought medical evaluation. Physical examination revealed a height of 175 cm, weight of 80 kg, and a BMI of 26.1, indicating slight obesity. Local examination showed bloody discharge from a single duct in each of the bilateral nipples. No palpable masses were detected in the breasts or areolas, and the axillary lymph nodes were not palpable.

Mammography revealed scattered microcalcifications in the left breast. There were no abnormal findings for the right breast. Ultrasonography showed a hypo-echoic lesion of 3 mm in diameter in C region of the left breast, and the right breast showed duct dilatation in C region. Fine-needle aspiration cytology showed class V for both the left and right breasts, and smear cytology also showed class V for both breasts. Blood tests showed no abnormalities. Hormone tests gave the following results: LH 25.5 mIU/ml (normal range: 1.1~8.8), FSH 33.6 mIU/ml (1.8~13.6), PRL 18.8 ng/ml (3.6~12.8), E1 96.2 pg/ml (10~90), E2 28.1 pg/ml (20~60.1), E3 ≤ 5 pg/ml (≤ 5), testosterone 4.11 ng/ml (2.7–11) and free-testosterone 9.1 pg/ml (6.9–18.4). LH and FSH were high, and PRL was slightly elevated. E1 was slightly elevated, whereas E2, E3, testosterone and free testosterone were normal. In the LHRH loading test, LH and FSH increased normally, but testosterone and estrogen showed poor responses. In the hCG loading test, testosterone showed a baseline (preloading) value of 4.82 ng/ml and then increased only slightly to 7.41 ng/ml after loading. A chromosomal study showed a normal male karyotype of 46XY. Pelvic MRI examination showed the bilateral scrota to be filled with a water-density mass, and there were no clear findings characteristic of testes.

What is the most likely diagnosis?
